aboutH2: Sober Maintenance: one-to-one recovery coaching in Toronto
intro: Sober Maintenance is a private addiction recovery coaching service in Toronto, run by certified addiction counsellor and recovery coach Trevor Smith. It is not a rehab centre and there is no facility. Trevor works with one client at a time, in person at home, at a cottage or in a hotel anywhere in the GTA, and by video, phone and text in between.

The work is built for adults who want to stop or cut back on alcohol, drugs or gambling and are ready to put in daily effort. Some come before a crisis, wanting discretion and structure instead of a facility intake. Others have finished treatment, or relapsed more than once, and want support shaped around their own life. Medical detox, psychotherapy and crisis care are outside its scope.

pillars.title: Training, not treatment
pillars.body: Trevor calls his approach the ART Method, for Addiction Recovery Training. He treats sobriety as a skill that has to be practised, so the work goes beyond talking about why addiction happens. It rests on three foundations, motivation, mindfulness and meaning, and nine training disciplines: journalling, neuro-psychoeducation, trauma-informed learning, mindfulness, yoga and movement, Buddhist philosophy, a genogram workshop, relapse realization and rigid accountability. He avoids the phrase relapse prevention. A relapse, in his view, is something to study honestly and without shame, because it shows which thoughts, places and needs led there. He is also upfront that training is slower than treatment, and that it asks for daily effort nobody else can do for you.

pillars.title: Recovery where you actually live
pillars.body: Sessions happen where your life happens: your house in Toronto, a cottage, a hotel suite, a walking trail or a video call between meetings. The 30-day program pairs five full days of in-person coaching, about eight hours each, with ten virtual counselling sessions and daily check-ins by text, email or phone. Longer programs of 60 or 90 days start with several virtual sessions, move to an in-home intensive, then taper into daily virtual contact and a slower integration phase. For clients who need the most discretion, Trevor offers live-in sober companionship and travel support, priced by the day.

pillars.title: One coach with lived experience
pillars.body: There is no rotating staff at Sober Maintenance. Trevor Smith keeps a small caseload and is the only person clients deal with, from the first email to the last session. He is a certified addiction counsellor (CCAC) and recovery coach (CCRC), with an Honours BA in cognitive science from the University of Toronto, where he studied under John Vervaeke and Jordan Peterson, and a graduate certificate in addictions and mental health from Durham College. He worked for almost four years as a primary counsellor at a private treatment centre and teaches in a college addictions program. He spent 30 years working in casinos and the gambling trade, and has been sober since September 2019.

overview: Sober Maintenance offers addiction counselling and recovery coaching for alcohol, cocaine and other stimulants, cannabis, methamphetamine and poly-substance use, with particular depth in gambling problems that come alongside drinking or drug use. It accepts people aiming for full abstinence and people trying to reduce harm or cut back. Trevor uses motivational interviewing and borrows from CBT, DBT and ACT, while saying he does not claim to specialize in any one of them.

Clients pick the shape of support. Single sessions are pay as you go, monthly coaching gives a steady weekly rhythm, and the 30-day hybrid program works as an intensive alternative for people who do not want to enter a facility. Longer 60 and 90-day programs are planned together over several virtual sessions before any in-home days are booked.

Sober Maintenance does not offer medical detox, psychiatric care, diagnosis, psychotherapy or emergency help, and Trevor is not a licensed psychotherapist. Someone in acute withdrawal, with active psychosis or at risk of self-harm should go to a hospital or call 911. Coaching can start once that care is in place, or run alongside it.

location.intro: Sober Maintenance has no public office. Trevor Smith is based in Toronto and travels to clients across the GTA, so Mississauga, Vaughan and Markham are usually 30 to 45 minutes away by car, and Oakville or Ajax closer to 45 minutes. Hamilton and Oshawa are about an hour, and anything farther is done by video or as a destination engagement with travel billed separately.

faqIntro: Answers come from the Sober Maintenance website and its recovery.com profile. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Sober Maintenance a residential rehab?
faqs.a: No. Sober Maintenance is a private, one-to-one recovery coaching and addiction counselling service with no beds and no facility. Trevor Smith comes to you at home, at a cottage, in a hotel or at a destination, and also works by video. If you need live-in treatment, compare residential centres in Toronto and across Ontario.

faqs.q: How much does Sober Maintenance cost?
faqs.a: A 60-minute virtual session is $175 and an in-person hour is $225, according to the Sober Maintenance website. Monthly coaching is $600 for four sessions or $1,120 for eight. The 30-day hybrid program is $5,900 CAD, longer 60 and 90-day programs start at about $15,000 and $20,000, and live-in sober companionship runs $1,200 to $2,000 a day plus travel.

No. The service does not include medical detox, psychiatric treatment, diagnosis, psychotherapy or emergency care. It is not meant for anyone with unmanaged withdrawal risk, psychosis or risk of self-harm. Trevor can discuss referrals, and coaching can start after or alongside medical care.

The 30-day hybrid program combines five days of in-person coaching, about eight hours a day, with ten virtual counselling sessions of 60 to 75 minutes. It also includes daily text, email or phone check-ins for the whole month, journal reflections and addiction education drawn from psychology, neuroscience and trauma-informed resources. It is available anywhere in the GTA.

Trevor Smith is based in Toronto and works in person across the Greater Toronto Area, in clients' homes, cottages or hotels. Virtual sessions can happen from anywhere, and the concierge service travels to a destination of the client's choosing, with travel and lodging billed separately. There is no public office address.

It is for adults who want to change their drinking, drug use or gambling and are willing to do daily work. Trevor works with people seeking full abstinence and with people trying to cut back, including high-functioning drinkers, poly-substance users and chronic relapsers. Many clients are professionals, executives or public figures who need privacy.

faqs.q: Can a family member book on someone's behalf?
faqs.a: Families can reach out for a consultation, but the person with the addiction has to want to change. Trevor states that this is not an intervention service. For concierge clients, a lawyer, physician, assistant or family member can make first contact, and an optional family track can run alongside the client's own work.

faqs.q: Is Sober Maintenance covered by insurance or OHIP?
faqs.a: No insurance is listed. Sober Maintenance is private pay, and the recovery.com profile lists it as private pay only. Trevor is not a licensed psychotherapist, so check with your extended health plan before assuming any session can be claimed.

faqs.q: What happens after a program ends?
faqs.a: Most clients move into monthly coaching, with a weekly session and regular check-ins by text and email. Longer programs include an integration phase where in-person days taper into virtual sessions. Concierge clients can continue on a private retainer, and the website also offers a free online workbook, Finding Meaning in Addiction Recovery.

faqs.q: How do I start with Sober Maintenance?
faqs.a: Start with a free, confidential 30-minute consultation, booked online or by email at trevor@sobermaintenance.com. Next comes a virtual interview to go over your history, and then you agree on a plan together. There is no waiting list or intake desk, and Trevor handles every inquiry himself.
